notes: nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b for LiteRT (litert-community/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b): nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b (revision ea30d66d, openmdw-1.1), a cache-aware streaming FastConformer encoder with an RNN-T decoder and a language prompt, rewritten as plain PyTorch graphs (no NeMo) and exported with litert-torch 0.10.0 for LiteRT 2.3.0 at lookahead 3 (320 ms chunks): mel, pre (the subsampling with its convolution caches), the 24-layer conformer with its attention and convolution caches as graph inputs and outputs, and the RNN-T decoder (predict, joint); the host carries the caches from chunk to chunk and runs the greedy RNN-T loop (at most 10 tokens per encoder frame). The float16 conformers scale each of their 144 LayerNorm inputs by 2^-k (k 2-9) so float16 arithmetic stays finite. Accuracy = WER (CER for FLEURS Japanese) against the reference: transformers 5.22.1 Nemotron3_5AsrForRNNT in float32 on the same chunks with the same 5,520 zeros appended, greedy decoding, each set's language-locale as the prompt; L = the Open ASR Leaderboard's scoring, J = jiwer on the same normalized text. This file: nemotron_asr_conformer_f16_cpu.tflite (1,217,291,232 B; the card's Files table: the 24-layer conformer for one chunk (`conformer`), its attention and convolution caches as inputs and outputs; float16 weights, its LayerNorm inputs rescaled so that float16 arithmetic does not overflow, and its relative-position matmuls written as fully connected layers so that XNNPACK runs its arithmetic in float16 (4,090 of the graph's 4,093 nodes; the three concatenations at its end stay on LiteRT's own CPU kernel); backend CPU). artifact_sha256 = = the work graph conformer_fp16ws_fc.tflite that the Mac runs loaded (their meta lines name it).
